page.layout: One page of text in one column: a short introductory paragraph, then a chronological table of years with consul names in braces, followed by prose lines between the table rows. main_text.l: Ut autem lectori id ipsum evidentius & quasi ad
oculum pateat, sequentem, quam subjicio, tabellam
An. ÆRÆ Vulg. | Vere. | Jul. per Jul. | U. C.
Augustus die Aug. xix. mortuus, Tiberium habuit
Tiberius annum egit 1 & 2 atque etiamnum Annius
Gratus mittitur in locum Annii. Ann. 1.

page.notes: Small dot marks stand to the left of the first year row and beside the consul line for 770 (possibly printer's marks or reference marks; no matching note on the page). A printer's dot also stands at the top of the page above the running head; it is an ornament and is left out. "Valerii Gratu ... 3." : the word may read "Grati"; marked [?]. The table braces are rendered as " | coss." after each pair of consuls. The last line "Tibe-" is the catchword and is printed once in bottom_margin; the duplicate in main_text should be treated as the catchword only.
